title: Regulation 3 - Definition and Scope of Ayurveda Aahar
section_title: Regulation 3 - Definition and Scope of Ayurveda Aahar
authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) & Ministry of AYUSH
publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
content: Regulation 3 defines 'Ayurveda Aahar' as food prepared in accordance with the recipes or ingredients or processes described in the authoritative books of Ayurveda listed in Schedule A, but shall not include Ayurvedic drugs, parenteral preparations, or products containing isolated chemical entities or synthetic vitamins/minerals.

title: Regulation 4 - General Principles and Permissible Ingredients
section_title: Regulation 4 - General Principles and Permissible Ingredients
authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) & Ministry of AYUSH
publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
content: Ayurveda Aahar products shall strictly contain botanical and dietary ingredients authorized under Schedule A. Products may be in conventional food formats (beverages, powders, cookies, syrups, ghee, candies) or modern supplement delivery formats (tablets, capsules) strictly intended for dietary nourishment and health promotion.

title: Regulation 6 - Labeling Requirements and Mandatory Warnings
section_title: Regulation 6 - Labeling Requirements and Mandatory Warnings
authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) & Ministry of AYUSH
publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
content: Mandatory labeling mandates: (1) Official green 'Ayurveda Aahar' logo on principal display panel; (2) Prominent disclaimer in bold: 'ONLY FOR DIETARY PURPOSES AND NOT FOR MEDICINAL USE'; (3) Target consumer group, recommended daily allowance, and dosha balance; (4) Absolute prohibition on claiming prevention, cure, or mitigation of specific diseases.

title: Regulation 8 - Quality and Safety Standards
section_title: Regulation 8 - Quality and Safety Standards
authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) & Ministry of AYUSH
publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
content: All Ayurveda Aahar products must comply with microbiological criteria, heavy metal tolerances (Lead <= 5ppm, Arsenic <= 1.1ppm, Mercury <= 0.25ppm, Cadmium <= 0.3ppm), pesticide residues, and aflatoxin limits specified in Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations.
